title: What if you had 8 fingers?
_map: Counting with 8 fingers (stretch). Big idea: we count in tens because we have ten fingers; other counting systems work too. Creative: invent a creature with a different number of fingers.
_story: Steve has only 8 fingers (4 on each hand), so it bundles carrots in groups of 8, not 10. Same carrots, different groups. Ismaeel tries bundling 23 carrots both ways and invents his own creature.
_stepChain: we have 10 fingers → so we bundle in tens (bundles-of-ten) → Steve has 8 fingers → it bundles in eights → 23 carrots = 2 tens and 3, or 2 eights and 7 → same carrots, different groups → invent a creature

talk.ask: Why do people count in tens?
talk.goodAnswer: because we have ten fingers, so bundling in tens was natural.
as 2 eights and 7: he bundles in eights because he has 8 fingers. Same carrots, different groups.

handsOn: Invent a creature with a different number of fingers, like 3 or 6. Draw it! Then grab some Lego bricks and bundle them the way your creature would count.

narration.text: Ismaeel, hold up your hands! Wiggle your fingers! How many? 10! That's why people count in tens. 10 fingers, then we start again with a new ten.
Here are 23 carrots. Let's bundle them in tens. 2 bundles of ten, and 3 left over!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Now let's pretend. In my blocky world, I've only got 4 fingers on each hand, like lots of cartoon characters! Count them: 8 fingers. So I count in eights! 8 fingers, then I start again with a new bundle of 8.
Can you help Steve bundle the 23 carrots in eights? Pick how many bundles of 8, then tap the hammer.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I made 2 eights and 7. You made 2 tens and 3. We got different answers! So one of us has more carrots. Is it me?

question.onRight: Yes! It's the same 23 carrots, bundled in different groups.

0.mistake: thinks bigger bundles mean more carrots
0.hint: Did any carrots get added, or munched? Or were they only bundled differently?
0.say: Nobody added a carrot, and nobody munched one! Tens or eights, it's still the same 23 carrots.

2.mistake: thinks more bundles or a bigger left-over number means more
2.hint: Steve's 7 is bigger than our 3. But are his bundles as big as ours?
2.say: Steve's bundles are smaller: eights, not tens. So he has more left over. But it's still the same 23 carrots!

question.reveal: 23 carrots either way! Counting in eights works, and counting in tens works too.

narration.text: Now you be the inventor! Imagine a funny creature with a different number of fingers. Maybe 3. Maybe 6! How would it bundle its carrots? Tell a grown-up all about your creature!

rule.text: We count in tens because we have 10 fingers.
rule.ask: Why do we count in tens? And how does Steve count? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: We count in tens because we have 10 fingers. Steve has 8 fingers, so he counts in eights. Both ways work.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! A creature with 5 fingers bundles in fives. How would it bundle 23 carrots?
bonus.reveal: 4 fives and 3! Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, and 3 more.
